entries.claim: If $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a polynomial in x, then the set of values of x which makes $f(x)=0$ is called the set of zeroes of the function f and is denoted by the symbol $Z(f)$.
entries.quote: the set of zeroes of the function f and its denoted by the sumbol Z (f).
entries.note: The definition is fully stated in the 'Generally' box: 'if f : R → R is a polynomial in x, then the set of values of x which makes f(x) = 0 is called the set of zeroes of the function f and is denoted by the symbol Z (f).'

entries.claim: Z(f) is the solution set of the equation f(x) = 0.
entries.quote: Z (f) is the solution set of the equation f (x) = 0
entries.note: The page explicitly states: 'i.e : Z (f) is the solution set of the equation f (x) = 0' below the Generally section.
